unit.why: The division mainly narrates how the Besht was lured to a feast by enemies who meant to kill him, was saved by apples and a yihud, and opened locked doors; it adds a brief allusion to his miraculous journey to Drohobych, all inside a homiletic frame about opposition to tsaddikim.
unit.boundary_note: Starts mid-sequence: a numbered section 'ו)' under the heading 'מענין תפוחים', excerpted from נ״מ שביל היחוד. Ends with a homiletic tail about the Maggid and opponents.

stories.start_quote: כמו שהיה למרן הבעש״ט שציערו אותו מאד
stories.summary_en: Enemies invite the Besht to a feast in order to get him drunk and kill him. Through apples and a yihud he stays sober while they fall into a deep sleep. He orders the locked doors to open, decrees punishment on them (postponed twenty years at their wives' tearful plea) and flees with miraculous speed, as in the known tale of his quick journey to R. Abba of Drohobych.
